padding_oracle_cbc.description: WSTG-CRYP-02 -- CBC-mode ciphertext (cookie, view-state, encrypted-token) reveals padding validity via differential response (200 vs 500, or distinct error text). Vaudenay attack: byte-level plaintext recovery + arbitrary ciphertext forging.

probes.description: Flip the last byte of a base64/hex ciphertext-looking value -- distinct response between 'padding invalid' (500) and 'mac/decrypt OK but business-logic fail' (400/200) reveals oracle. Confirm with 3 flipped variants.
Detect ASP.NET view-state padding oracle (CVE-2010-3332 lineage) -- ViewState parameter present + behaviour delta on flipped last byte

weak_hash_in_token.description: WSTG-CRYP-04 -- MD5/SHA-1 fingerprint visible in session token, CSRF token, reset-link signature. MD5 length=32 hex, SHA-1 length=40 hex -- collidable/preimage-attackable depending on use

probes.description: Response or cookie contains 32-hex-char value used as auth/CSRF token -- likely MD5 (collision-attackable for forgery)
Response or cookie contains 40-hex-char value used as auth/CSRF token -- likely SHA-1 (chosen-prefix collision practical since 2020)

weak_jwt_alg_hs256_with_predictable_secr.description: WSTG-CRYP-04 / WSTG-SESS-10 -- JWT signed with HS256 and short/predictable secret. Brute-forceable offline if secret is dictionary word, env-default, or service name

probes.description: JWT detected with HS256 -- pull token, attempt hashcat -m 16500 with rockyou + service-name-based wordlist offline. Tool layer flags presence; cracking is offline.

des_3des_rc4_in_response.description: WSTG-CRYP-04 -- response advertises DES / 3DES / RC4 / EXPORT cipher (Server header, Set-Cookie, custom debug). Often combined with weak TLS (WSTG-CRYP-01) audited offline via nmap.

probes.description: Response mentions DES/3DES/RC4/EXPORT/NULL cipher in debug header or body

encrypted_blob_without_integrity.description: Token looks encrypted (base64 long + high entropy) but client can modify and submit -- no HMAC over ciphertext. Reveals via padding-oracle or bit-flip giving 200 instead of 500.

probes.description: Flip a byte mid-ciphertext -- if server returns 200 (or distinct non-padding error) the blob is unauthenticated (no HMAC wrapper)

hash_length_extension.description: WSTG-CRYP hash length-extension -- server authenticates client-controlled data with a naive MAC = H(secret || message) using a Merkle-Damgard hash (MD5 / SHA-1 / SHA-256). Knowing only message, its MAC, and the secret LENGTH (often guessable/bruteable), an attacker forges a valid MAC for `message || padding || attacker_data` WITHOUT the secret -- appending e.g. `&admin=true` or `&role=1` to a signed request. Detection flags the signed-parameter shape (a hex MAC beside the data it signs); exploitation uses hashpumpy over a small length range. The fix is HMAC (H(secret,H(secret,message))), which is not extendable.

probes.description: Signed-parameter shape -- a hex MAC (32/40/64 chars = MD5/SHA1/SHA256) travels beside the data it authenticates. LEAD: if the MAC is H(secret||data) rather than HMAC, it is length-extension forgeable. Confirm the length range with hashpumpy, then append attacker params and replay.

ecb_mode_repeated_blocks.description: WSTG-CRYP-02 -- an encrypted token/cookie shows the ECB fingerprint: identical plaintext blocks encrypt to identical ciphertext blocks, so a repeated block appears verbatim in the ciphertext (a repeated 32-hex / 16-byte AES block run). Leaks structure and enables block cut-and-paste and byte-at-a-time recovery when the attacker controls adjacent plaintext. Detection is the shape; block-shuffle / byte-at-a-time exploitation is operator-driven.

probes.description: Repeated 16-byte block in a hex-encoded token (ECB signature) -- a 32-hex run recurs within the same value. LEAD: ciphertext is ECB (or a block mode leaking repeated blocks); structure leaks and cut-and-paste tampering is possible. Chance collision of a 128-bit block is negligible, so a repeat is real signal.

cbc_bitflip_tamper.description: WSTG-CRYP-02 -- a block-aligned ciphertext token (length a multiple of the 16-byte block) carries authorization/role/identity data with no integrity check (no HMAC/signature). In CBC mode flipping byte i of ciphertext block N deterministically flips byte i of plaintext block N+1 (garbling block N), so a role=user / admin=0 field can be tampered without the key. LEAD only -- the flip-and-replay is operator-driven; this flags the vulnerable shape (block-aligned ciphertext + no integrity marker).

probes.description: Block-aligned hex ciphertext (>=2 AES blocks, length a multiple of 32 hex) in an auth/role-bearing parameter, with no integrity marker in the response -- CBC bit-flip tamper candidate.

stream_cipher_iv_nonce_reuse.description: WSTG-CRYP-02 -- a stream cipher (CTR/OFB/CFB) or GCM used with a STATIC or all-zero IV/nonce reuses the keystream across messages. XOR of two same-keystream ciphertexts cancels the key (crib-drag plaintext recovery), and GCM nonce reuse additionally enables authentication-tag forgery. Flags a fixed/zero nonce exposed in a token or an explicit iv=/nonce= parameter; cross-request keystream comparison is the operator/tool confirmation step.

probes.description: All-zero or single-repeated-character IV/nonce in a parameter or token -- a fixed nonce reuses the keystream across messages (crib-drag recovery; GCM forgery). LEAD: confirm reuse by comparing the nonce across two captured requests.
